result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (6 tests, 0 failures — the stack traces printed during the run are the framework logging already-handled `ValidationException`s, same as before my change).

I added a public JSON feed at `GET /api/posts`. `routes/api.ts` is a new route module (called from `registerWebRoutes` in `routes/web.ts`, alongside `registerAuthRoutes`) that registers the route as `api.posts.index` with its contract declared on the route itself: `query: ApiListPostsQuerySchema` for the accepted parameters and `resource: { data: [PostResource] }` for the response shape, mirroring how `posts.search` is declared. `ApiListPostsQuerySchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` coerces the string query values — `page` (positive int, default 1) and optional `author` (positive int) — so `?page=2&author=3` parses while `page=0`, `page=abc`, `author=abc` and `author=0` fail and surface as a 422 JSON body. The handler is a new `app/Http/Controllers/Api/PostController.ts`, kept apart from the Inertia `PostController` since it renders no page; it re-validates the same schema, then counts and slices by hand (`count()` + `limit`/`offset` on fresh builders) rather than using `paginate({ page })`, because that ORM path resolves no eager loads and the contract requires `author` on every post — the site's own `/posts` page has the same gap today, which I left alone. It returns `{ data, meta, links }` built from `PostResource` and the `paginate()` helper, with the author filter carried into the page links. `bun run codegen` regenerated `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, where the route now appears as `api.posts.index` with `response: { data: Array<Data.Post> }`. Tests live in `tests/ApiPostController.test.ts` (read-only, so they don't disturb the shared test database), and I documented the endpoint in `README.md`.
